transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-27
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Owen (Redwood SE), Alex (Northbridge Platform), Priya (CTO), Jordan (DevOps), Sofia (Procurement)

Summary:
Quick renewal check-in to confirm capacity uplift, discuss adding EU regions (Frankfurt), clarify data residency and security concerns, and plan a small Dedicated pilot to validate latency/cost tradeoffs before contract amendment.

Topics: renewal timeline, capacity numbers, EU activation, Dedicated pilot, SOC2/KMS, pricing model, procurement next steps

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roundtable — how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Alex: good, thanks. busy quarter for us, but ready to lock next steps for the inference platform.
[00:14] Priya: hi all. main thing for me today is timeline — need EU up by July for a compliance rollout.
[00:20] Jordan: and we want predictable latency under 120ms p95 for our chat endpoints, otherwise ops will escalate.
[00:27] Owen: got it. we did some numbers on our side, should be doable with Dedicated in eu-west, depends on batch sizing and kv cash — sorry kv cache — and quantization profile.
[00:38] Alex: kv cash ha — yep we saw that in the last report, haha.
[00:42] Maya: so quick recap — current commit ends end of June, you're at about 20M tokens / month, and you mentioned wanting a 2x bump to start plus enabling Frankfurt region. correct?
[00:53] Jordan: yes, that's right. 40M tokens would be comfortable as the committed tier, with burst credits for peak traffic.
[00:59] Priya: we also need to confirm data residency for logs and KV cache snapshots, and that encryption keys remain customer-controlled via KMS.
[01:07] Owen: absolutely. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS in the VPC flow; Dedicated can also be configured to send audit logs to your SIEM.
[01:14] Priya: do you have the SOC2 report and network diagram handy? we've started security review.
[01:19] Maya: yes, we'll share the security pack after the call — SOC2, ISO stub, and a redacted network diagram.

[01:35] Owen: as for the latency target, two levers: hosted versus Dedicated, and model variant. For eu-west, Dedicated with 1:1 capacity for your peak path should hit ~90-110ms p95 depending on sequence length and concurrency. If you use a quantized variant and set continuous batching at 20ms window, that improves throughput at small latency cost.
[01:58] Jordan: when you say 1:1 capacity, what does that mean for cost? we need unit economics vs CloudML.
[02:05] Maya: we'll put a clear per-token equivalent and reserved capacity table in the addendum. early view: Dedicated committed tiers reduce effective per-token by ~30% versus bursty hosted at scale, but there's a minimum monthly commitment.
[02:19] Sofia: procurement question — do you support SSO / SAML for console access? we need RBAC and SCIM sync.
[02:26] Owen: yes SAML + SCIM, RBAC at token/route level, and audit logs with retention options. small note: sometimes SAML attributes mapping needs tweaking, we've helped customers with a one-hour setup session.

[02:45] Alex: competitor check — we've been talking to ModelServeX and CloudML endpoints. main difference for us is how well the platform handles high-throughput caching and cost controls.
[02:56] Maya: good to know. Redwood Optimize recommendations and the Console's cost breakdown are often a deciding factor for teams looking to lower unit economics while preserving quality.

[03:12] Priya: for the pilot — what's the minimal scope you'd recommend to validate EU latency and cost?
[03:17] Owen: I'd propose a 10-business-day Dedicated pilot in Frankfurt: mirror 1% of production traffic (or synthetic 2k qps if you can't share prod), run p50/p90/p95 latency, per-token cost, and model quality checks on a small prompt set you provide. We can do KV caching enabled and a couple of quantization profiles.
[03:36] Jordan: we can provide a 1-week production telemetry dump. synthetic test is ok too if we need quicker results.

[03:45] Maya: timeline check — if we start pilot second week of May, bench report by end of May, contract addendum by early June, you could have EU live mid-July. does that align with your July compliance deadline?
[03:58] Priya: yes mid-July is tight but workable if procurement moves fast.
[04:03] Sofia: procurement will need the pricing spreadsheet and a one-page SOW for the commitment before legal can draft an addendum.
[04:10] Maya: we'll send those. I'll include burst credit mechanics and a tiered table that shows committed tokens, burst allowance, and overage rates.

[04:25] Owen: one technical caveat — for very low-latency workloads, prefix caching and small-batch windows matter a lot. if you have many short prompts, we'll recommend smaller batch windows and a higher ratio of dedicated endpoints to avoid queuing.
[04:40] Jordan: our chat endpoints are largely short prompts, so that guidance is helpful. do you support sticky routing by customer region so EU traffic stays in EU?
[04:48] Owen: yes, smart routing policies can pin by region and fall back to another variant if capacity's constrained. there is also an auto-failover option.

[05:02] Priya: security follow-up — keys: we need an HSM/KMS option and ability to rotate keys regularly without downtime.
[05:10] Owen: supported. rotation can be orchestrated via your KMS and we provide guidance to avoid cache invalidation windows.

[05:20] Maya: okay let's recap next steps before we wrap.
[05:24] Maya: Action items — I will send draft addendum + pricing + security pack by May 1. Owen will prep the Dedicated EU pilot config and run the synthetic benchmark if needed by May 11. Jordan will provide the one-week telemetry by May 4. Priya/Sofia will confirm procurement timeline and sign-off owners by May 6.
[05:45] Priya: thanks, that works. any blockers on Redwood's side?
[05:49] Maya: nothing big. just internal capacity scheduling for the pilot but we've reserved a window.
[05:55] Alex: happy with plan. please include the telemetry schema that Jordan needs to export.
[06:00] Owen: I'll share a small telemetry spec and a sample ingestion script.
[06:06] Maya: great — we'll follow up in email and I'll create the calendar for the pilot kickoff. Thanks everyone.
[06:12] Sofia: thanks.
[06:14] All: bye.

Recap (final bullets):
- Customer wants 2x committed tokens (20M -> 40M) + EU (Frankfurt) activation by mid-July.
- Pilot: Dedicated EU, 10 business days, synthetic 2k qps or 1% mirrored prod, evaluate p50/p95 and cost.
- Security: share SOC2/ISO and KMS/HSM options; customer needs KMS control and audit logs.
- Procurement needs pricing spreadsheet and SOW; Redwood to supply by 2026-05-01.

References mentioned during call:
- Link: /redwood/security-pack (SOC2 + network diagram) [will be shared]
- Benchmark template: /redwood/pilot/benchmark-template.xlsx [Owen to populate]

End of transcript.
